info.name: Vertex Commerce API
info.description:
Backend API for the Vertex Commerce admin panel and customer storefronts (Platforms).

**Usage guide:** [/api-docs/guide](https:///api-docs/guide) explains where to start and the order of the calls.

**Surfaces**

- `/api/v1/admin/\*` — admin panel. Bearer token (Sanctum) + per-action permissions.
    
- `/api/v1/store/\*` — storefront (Nuxt). Platform credential header. The platform is resolved from the credential, never from the payload.  
    Call these endpoints from the Nuxt **server** (BFF / server routes) only — never expose the secret to the browser.
    

**Conventions**

- Money: integer JPY. Time: ISO 8601 UTC in responses; instants sent to the API must carry a UTC offset (RFC 3339); business dates (`date`) are Asia/Tokyo.
    
- Lists use cursor pagination (`cursor`, `limit`) and return `meta.next_cursor`.
    
- Mutations on versioned resources require `lock_version`; mismatch → 409 `stale_version`.
    
- `Idempotency-Key` header is required on bulk operations and variant generation (missing → 422 `errors.Idempotency-Key`). Keys are remembered for 24 hours per principal and route: the same key and body return the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; a different body → 409 `idempotency_conflict`; a request still running → 409 `idempotency_in_progress`; a 5xx response is not stored, so the client may retry with the same key.
    
- Errors use the `Error` envelope. 422 → per-field `errors`.
    
- Every success body is `{ data: … }`; lists add `meta` (`next_cursor`, `total`, and list-level extras such as `facets` or `scope`). There are no other top-level keys: tokens, secrets and job ids are inside `data`.
    
- Create returns `201 { data: }`; update returns `200 { data: }`.
    
- Lists accept `include_total=true` to add `meta.total` (costly; use only when the UI shows a count).
    
- Admin operations declare the required permission in `x-permission`. Missing permission → 403 `forbidden`.
    
- Long operations return `202 { data: { job_id, status_url } }`; poll `GET /admin/jobs/{job}`.
    
- Files are uploaded first via `POST /admin/uploads` (pre-signed); resources reference the returned `upload_id`.
    
- A response only contains the data of its own resource. Related records of other resources are fetched through their own list endpoint with a filter (e.g. `GET /admin/products?category_id=`).

item.name: Override or reset the content of one platform, field by field

request.description:
A field sent in the body is overridden on this platform; a field listed in `reset` follows Default again; the other fields are left as they are. Send at least one field or `reset` → otherwise 422 `required_without_all` (field `reset`); a `reset` value that is not a field → 422 `in` (`reset.{i}`). The same categories in another order are no change.
Overriding needs the platform to be assigned to the product (a variant: to its parent) → 422 `platform_not_assigned` (field `platform`); `reset` alone also works for a platform that is no longer assigned. A field both sent and reset → 422 `override_and_reset` (field `reset.{i}`).
`name` needs English, like the Default name. `notes: null` means no notes on this platform. `media` replaces the platform images: keep or reorder by `id` (an image of this platform, or a Default image of the product, which is copied), add by `upload_id`; an empty list means no images on this platform; without a base image the first one is the base. `category_ids` may be empty (no category on this platform); unknown categories → 422 `not_found` (`category_ids.{i}`); variants follow the categories of their parent → 422 `field_inherited`. On a platform, a category holds only the products assigned to that platform.
The SKU is global, the same on every platform whatever the platform name: `sku` in the body, even empty or null → 422 `prohibited`. The other settings are global too (updateProduct).
The platform content has its own `lock_version` (0 while nothing is overridden); stale → 409 `stale_version`. A trashed product → 409 `product_trashed`. When the last overridden field is reset, the platform follows Default again in full and its `lock_version` returns to 0.

**Examples** (Tourist SIM 15GB on SK SIM, in order): 1. the first override sends `lock_version: 0`, names it Japan Tourist SIM 15GB, keeps the Default base image by its `id` (copied, so it gets a new id), adds an upload and lists it in SIM Cards as well as Tourist SIM; 2. `notes: null` overrides the notes with none while `reset` makes the categories follow Default again; 3. resetting the last overridden fields removes the override. The 422 example overrides on Old Store, which is no longer assigned to the product. Read the current `lock_version` of each platform from getProductPlatformContent.

request.description:
Creates the selected variants as simple child products (`parent_id`). Large sets run as a job (202).
This endpoint only creates variants: prices of new variants are set afterwards through the price-plan endpoints (`POST /admin/price-plans/bulk`, one line set for all variants, or per variant).
On a simple → configurable conversion, the simple product's price is copied to the new variants shortly after the response (asynchronously).
If the product is simple, the system converts it to configurable (it keeps its SKU, which becomes the parent SKU and is no longer sellable);
`subscription_target_combination` is required when it has active subscriptions or bundles contain it (422 `required`, `not_selected`).
Every bundle selection holding the product then holds the target variant (same selection id, so its in-bundle price stays); the selection stays hidden while the variant is not active — nothing is activated automatically.
Generated names are `{parent name} - {labels}`; a new combination without `sku` gets a generated SKU (`{PARENT SKU}-{OPTION CODE}-…`, axes in attribute id order). New variants of a parent that has left Draft start inactive (they have no price yet).
Combination errors: `combinations.{i}.option_ids` → `invalid_combination`, `distinct`; `combinations.{i}.sku` → `sku_taken`, `sku_duplicate`, `sku_invalid` (a generated SKU that is not available: send one), `field_locked`. Every SKU that cannot be used is reported in the same 422, one field per combination, and nothing is created.
Sets that create more than 100 variants run as the `variant_generate` job (202).

response.name: OK

request.description:
Partial update of the Default values; same validation as create. Per-platform Name, Notes, Images and Categories go through updateProductPlatformContent; the other settings are global. `type` cannot change (only simple → configurable via variants/generate).
Locked fields after leaving draft → 422 `field_locked`. Status changes go through POST /status.
While Draft the SKU can change: a SKU claimed by a product that has left Draft → 422 `sku_taken`; the SKU of the product itself or of another of its variants (parent included) → `sku_duplicate`. Other Drafts may share it.
**Variants** accept only their own fields: name, sku (while the parent is Draft), notes, description, stock_status, attributes, reset_attribute_ids, media.
Inherited fields (categories, platforms, is_subscription, is_gift, requires_shipping) → 422 `field_inherited`. Configurable parents reject stock_status → 422 `stock_status_computed`; on a bundle `out_of_stock` forces it Out of Stock and `in_stock` lifts the force (the stock is otherwise computed from its contents).
List fields replace the whole list: `category_ids`, `platform_ids`, `attributes` (own values; a variant cannot set an axis attribute → 422 `axis_attribute`) and `media` (keep images by `id`, add by `upload_id`; without a base image the first one is the base).
`reset_attribute_ids` on a non-variant → 422 `variants_only`. A trashed product → 409 `product_trashed`; stale `lock_version` → 409.

request.description:
For the Create page: from the parent SKU and name and the chosen attribute options, returns every combination with its generated name and SKU and the status of that SKU. Nothing is stored and no SKU is reserved; uniqueness is checked again when the product is created.
SKUs are `{PARENT SKU}-{OPTION CODE}-…` with the axes in attribute id order (creation order), whatever the order of `axes`; the option code is the English label in upper case without spaces or characters a SKU cannot hold (`WIFI-X1` + Validity `8 Days` + Color `Black` → `WIFI-X1-8DAYS-BLACK`). Names are `{parent name} - {labels}` with the labels in the order of `axes`.
`combinations` (optional) checks SKUs the admin edited: a combination that matches a candidate replaces its SKU. A SKU that is not available is flagged, never changed.

1. The admin enters the parent SKU and name and picks the attributes and options → call this endpoint and show `candidates` (name, `suggested_sku`, `sku_status`) in the variant table.
2. The admin edits a SKU in the table → call it again with `combinations` (the `option_ids` of that row and the edited `sku`) to check it; repeat until every row to create is `available`. Here `WIFI-X1-16DAYS-WHITE` is already claimed by a released product (the trashed Pocket WiFi Router X1 (2023)), so it is replaced by `WIFI-X1-16D-WHT`.

request.description:
Out of stock products are included with stock_status. Variants are never listed; a configurable shows `price_from` of its active variants.
Price sorting uses a price index that updates shortly after a price change; the product detail always shows the current price.
Names, images and categories are the platform's: `q` and `sort=name` use the platform name, and `category_id` uses the categories of each product on this platform.
Without `sort`: with `category_id`, the product sort of that category on this platform, also given by storeListCategories, else newest first; a `sort` sent wins. `meta.sort` is the sort applied. `sort=position` / `-position` follow the platform's product order of `category_id` (direct assignments only; products without a place last in both directions), otherwise newest first; a category disabled on this platform or by Default (itself or an ancestor) → 404. Unknown filter codes are ignored. Facet counts ignore the attribute filters.
`price` is set for Single products; `price_from` is the cheapest active variant of a configurable, or for a bundle its base price plus the cheapest product of each required option.
